title: Console residency settings: backend endpoints + UI integration (pinning + violation summaries)
creator: Dylan Brooks
description:
Overview
Console needs first-class controls for Hosted/Dedicated data residency enforcement: (1) let authorized admins configure region pinning on an org/project, and (2) show a lightweight “recent violations” summary to support troubleshooting and compliance evidence. This ticket covers the Console backend endpoints and the end-to-end integration with the Region Pinning settings UI (DES-211), including wiring feature flags, RBAC, validation, and pulling violation summaries.

Context / Why
Enterprise customers are asking for EU-only processing guarantees and want to (a) self-serve residency configuration and (b) see whether enforcement is working (or why requests are being denied). Support is currently fielding tickets like “we enabled beta and now US endpoint requests are denied” — Console should make the mismatch obvious and provide remediation guidance.

Scope
1) Backend API for Console to read/update residency settings
- Add Console service endpoints that proxy to the control plane policy/config service (ENG-2841) for:
  - GET current residency policy effective at org/project/workspace scope
  - PATCH/PUT updates (pinned_region / allowed_regions / allow_cross_region_fallback override if enabled)
  - Validation errors mapped to the standardized error taxonomy (Confluence error-codes-data-residency)
- Enforce RBAC permissions (see rbac-policy-bundle PR 188):
  - Manage residency settings: compliance admin / org admin
  - View violation summaries: read-only compliance viewer permitted
- Audit trail: emit “residency.policy_updated” audit event (Console-initiated change) in addition to control-plane config audit logs (GRC wants provenance).

2) Violation summaries endpoint for Console
- Add endpoint for the Console UI to fetch “recent residency enforcement outcomes” for the org/project:
  - Focus: last 24h by default, plus quick presets (1h, 7d) to align with on-call/support workflows
  - Summary, not full event stream (full events live in audit log export). This is a UX/triage view.
- Data source: query the telemetry store populated by residency enforcement instrumentation (ENG-2845) and/or audit events (ENG-2844). Decision: use the aggregated metrics table for counts + link-out to audit log search for raw samples.

3) UI integration
- Wire DES-211 UI to:
  - Read current policy state
  - Update policy with inline validation + display warning copy
  - Render “recent violations” cards (count, most common reason, regions involved)
- Feature flag gating (ENG-2849 / residency_enforcement_console_settings):
  - Entire settings page or the mutation controls should be hidden behind flag for beta cohorts
  - Read-only display can be enabled earlier if desired for pilots

Non-goals
- Building a general audit log explorer in Console.
- Migrating historical artifacts or verifying downstream storage residency (handled elsewhere).

API Contract (Console ↔ Console Backend)
Routes (proposed, internal Console API; exact routing to follow existing Console conventions):
- GET /api/console/v1/orgs/:orgId/residency
- PATCH /api/console/v1/orgs/:orgId/residency
- GET /api/console/v1/orgs/:orgId/residency/violations?scope=org|project&scopeId=...&window=1h|24h|7d

Payload shape (documented here as text; implement as typed structs in console-backend):
- ResidencyPolicy fields:
  - mode: "pinned" | "allowed" | "none" (derived)
  - pinned_region: e.g., "eu-west" (nullable)
  - allowed_regions: comma-separated list, e.g., "eu-west,eu-central" (nullable)
  - effective_scope: "org" | "project" | "workspace" and id
  - updated_by: actor id/email (if available)
  - updated_at: RFC3339
  - enforcement_state: "disabled" | "enabled" (based on rollout flags + org tier)
  - allow_cross_region_fallback: "true" | "false" (if feature-flagged and exception-granted)

Validation rules to enforce (server-side; UI should pre-validate but not rely on it):
- pinned_region must be a member of allowed_regions if both set.
- allowed_regions must be from supported Hosted regions list.
- pinned_region XOR allowed_regions for MVP (ADR-042 clarifies precedence; if both set, pinned takes precedence but we should warn and/or normalize).
- Dedicated: if org has Dedicated-only deployment, allowed/pinned limited to provisioned Dedicated region(s); return actionable error.

Error mapping
Console backend should map control plane/gateway errors into consistent response format:
- HTTP 400 for validation errors, with machine error code from error-codes-data-residency where applicable.
- HTTP 403 for RBAC denied.
- HTTP 409 if update conflicts with concurrent edits (etag-based if available; otherwise last-write-wins with audit logging).

Violation Summaries
Return fields (summary-level):
- total_requests_checked
- total_denied
- denial_rate
- top_denial_reasons (e.g., RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH, RESIDENCY_POLICY_NOT_FOUND)
- denied_by_request_region (map as string: "us-east=12, eu-west=0" for now; UI can parse)
- pinned_region (echo)
- time_window
- last_seen_at
- sample_audit_event_ids (up to N ids; link-out to audit logs page / support instructions)

Implementation notes
- Permission checks:
  - Use the new RBAC permission keys added in rbac-policy-bundle/pr_188.
  - Ensure we don’t expose violation summaries to users without “view compliance telemetry” access.
- Caching:
  - GET residency policy can be cached for short TTL (30–60s) to reduce load; but PATCH should invalidate.
  - Violation summaries can be cached for 60s to avoid spamming metrics store.
- Observability:
  - Emit metrics: console_residency_settings_get_total, console_residency_settings_update_total{result=success|error}, console_residency_violations_query_total
  - Add trace attributes: org_id, scope, pinned_region (if set)
- Audit:
  - Emit audit event for config changes initiated via Console: include previous_policy and new_policy serialized as strings to avoid nested payload restrictions downstream.

Acceptance Criteria
- Console user with correct RBAC can:
  1) View current residency policy (including effective scope and pinned/allowed regions).
  2) Update residency policy; UI shows success toast and refreshed state.
  3) See recent violation summary for last 24h (and 1h/7d).
- Console user without RBAC:
  - Settings controls hidden or disabled; direct API calls return 403.
- Validation behavior:
  - Invalid region values return HTTP 400 with clear message and a stable error code.
- Feature flag:
  - When residency_enforcement_console_settings flag off, page does not allow edits (and optionally is fully hidden depending on product decision).

Testing
- Unit tests:
  - Validation mapping, RBAC checks, error translation.
- Integration tests:
  - Happy path: GET → PATCH → GET returns updated value.
  - Denied path: user without permission.
  - Violation summaries endpoint returns data and is stable under empty datasets.
- Staging verification:
  - Enable for one pilot org pinned to eu-west; confirm UI shows pinned region and violation summary increments when sending traffic to US endpoint.

Rollout Plan (Console-specific)
- Week 1: land backend endpoints + RBAC + feature flag; enable in staging.
- Week 2: enable for internal dogfood orgs; add support-facing screenshots.
- Beta: enable for pilot cohort aligned with PM-482; monitor console error rates + policy update volume.

Open questions
- Source of truth for “recent violations”: metrics store aggregation vs audit-event query. Current proposal: metrics for summary + audit IDs for evidence drilldown.
- Where to link “View details” from Console: public docs vs internal runbook. Suggest docs link for customers + “Contact Support” CTA.

Recent updates
- 2025-02-18 (Chloe Martin): Backend endpoints implemented behind feature flag; awaiting final RBAC permission string names from rbac-policy-bundle/pr_188.
- 2025-02-24 (Felix Schneider): UI expects violations endpoint to return both total_denied and last_seen_at; updated contract above.
- 2025-03-01 (Brian Murphy): Please ensure error payload includes remediation hint (“Check your API base URL / SDK region”) for RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH; align copy with PR 18519.
